tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document and public artifacts cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

base_version.description: The version id these edits apply to: the live version, as get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result returned it.

new_text.description: The text to put in its place; empty deletes old_text.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__list_artifacts
tools.description: List artifacts in your organization that you can open: your own, then those shared with you or that you have viewed, most recent first; with shared_only, only the latter. With type, lists instead the artifacts made from that type that you can open, your organization's included, without version ids; the default, if there is one, is first and marked.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours that is not public. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

base_version.description: Required when republishing: the version this publish replaces.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

as.description: The path the file is served at, e.g. index.html or css/site.css. Its extension says what it is served as.

path.description: Give this: the file's absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run.

uri.description: Leave out: the client fills it in.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the tab icon. Pass one when creating.

mode.description: For a republish; leave it out when creating. patch (default): only the files named change. replace: the files named are the whole artifact, and every other file is dropped.

remove.description: For a republish: served paths to delete, spelled as list_files gives them. A path the artifact does not hold is ignored without an error. To delete and change nothing else, give files as an empty list.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups) or 'org' (the user's whole organization). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB. A public artifact is not republished here: the owner publishes it from claude.ai or Claude Code.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB. A public artifact is not republished here: the owner publishes it from claude.ai or Claude Code.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups) or 'org' (the user's whole organization). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. There wasn't a written plan before; the IUP/TUI work existed only as the prompts for saga steps 24–27. I've now written one at `docs/iup-plan.md` and committed it on `feat/local-components` (`c4a8c88`). The fast gate passed. It is high level only; the components, crates, modules and files come after the sw-checklist work, as you asked.

**What the plan covers:**
- **Goal:** existing Reva GUI programs run unchanged in the browser, the desktop app and the live demo. `lib/ui/iup`, `lib/ui/gui` and the programs are not edited.
- **Decisions:** we reimplement in Rust the part of IUP's C API that Reva calls, as a virtual library like iconv and SQLite. Nothing is wrapped or redistributed. A Rust/Yew renderer draws it. The work lives in reva-fork and starts after the component restructuring.
- **Scope, measured:** 21 programs (the 20 in `examples/iup/` plus CoSy's `Tui.f`) use 70 of `lib/ui/gui`'s 136 words and about 75 IUP C functions. `Tui.f` alone needs 33 words: the basic controls and layout, text editing with F-keys, the file-open dialog, and popup/show/hide.
- **Work, in order:**
  1. **UI model:** IUP's element tree, attributes and layout in Rust, with no VM and no rendering.
  2. **The `iup` virtual library:** handles are integers. The event loop pauses the VM the same way SQLite calls do in the desktop app, and a headless host drives events in tests.
  3. **The Yew renderer:** for the web page and the desktop app.
  4. **`Tui.f` end to end.**
  5. **The remaining examples:** in order of how many programs each feature unblocks. Drawing, images and OpenGL come last.
- **How we'll know it works:** CLI goldens with scripted events, the web smoke test, manual checks in Chrome and the desktop app, and the parity report as the IUP examples go from failing to running.
- **Open questions:** whether the CLI gets no GUI or a terminal renderer, which look to use, how windows behave, where drawing goes, and recording the licensing in `docs/licenses.md`.
- **Risks:** IUP's layout rules are detailed, callback-heavy programs stress the pause/resume path, and the scope could creep.

PR #51 has been merged, so step 17 (`local-components`) can start. The plan commit will go into that step's PR unless you'd rather have it as its own PR now.

# reva-fork -- Claude Instructions

## Baseline expectations for agentrail-driven sessions

You are working with the agentrail saga/steps process. The saga record (the
`.agentrail/` directory) is the durable handoff between sessions — if your
work is not reflected there, the next session cannot see it.

Before reporting work as complete:

- Confirm the active step is reflected in `.agentrail/` and committed.
- Run the project's pre-commit gate (tests, lint, format) before
  `agentrail complete`, not after.
- If you discover unplanned work, prefer `agentrail insert` / `agentrail add`
  over silently doing it inside another step.

## CRITICAL: Agentrail session protocol (follow exactly)

Every session follows this sequence. Do not skip steps, do not reorder.

### 1. START — `agentrail next`
First thing in the session. Read the output carefully: it tells you the
current step number, prompt, skill docs, and past trajectories. If `next`
exits non-zero, the saga is complete or absent — do not invent work.

### 2. BEGIN — `agentrail begin`
Run immediately after reading `next` output. This transitions the step from
Pending to InProgress so the recorded history matches what actually
happened.

### 3. WORK
Do what the step prompt says. Do NOT ask the user "want me to proceed?" or
"shall I start?" — the step prompt IS your instruction. Execute it.

### 4. COMMIT
Commit your code changes with git BEFORE running `agentrail complete`.
The commit recorded into the step's `commits` field comes from `HEAD` at
the moment of `complete`, so the commit must land first.

### 5. COMPLETE — `agentrail complete`
```
agentrail complete --summary "what you accomplished" \
  --reward 1 \
  --actions "tools and approach used"
```
On failure: `--reward -1 --failure-mode "what went wrong"`.
On final step: add `--done`.

### 6. STOP
After `complete`, do NOT make further code changes. Anything after
`complete` is untracked and invisible to the next session. If you see more
work to do, it belongs in the NEXT step, not this one.

## Agentrail metadata discipline

When using agentrail, changes to `.agentrail/` files are first-class project
changes — the same as application source code. They must be committed, and
should be pushed before you hand off.

Before running `agentrail complete`:

1. `git status` — confirm `.agentrail/` files are tracked, not just present.
   Untracked files in `.agentrail/` mean the next session will not see them.
2. Stage and commit source changes and `.agentrail/` metadata together. The
   commit recorded into the step's `commits` field comes from `HEAD` at the
   moment of `agentrail complete`, so the commit must happen *first*.
3. Run `agentrail complete` after the commit lands.
4. Push the branch (or note the unpushed branch state in your handoff).

This is the most common agentrail failure mode: agents do the work, commit
the source, and forget the `.agentrail/` files. The result is a saga whose
recorded history disagrees with git history, which `agentrail audit` will
flag — but only after the damage is done.

### What's hand-editable in `.agentrail/`

Three categories of files live here, and the rules differ:

- **Append-only saga state** — `saga.toml`, `step.toml`, `plan.md`, session
  JSONLs under `sessions/`, trajectory JSONs under `trajectories/`, and
  anything under `.agentrail-archive/`. **Never hand-edit or delete these.**
  They are written by agentrail commands and represent the durable saga
  record; hand-editing desyncs the saga from git history and from prior
  session memory. A direct `rm` on untracked files is unrecoverable.
- **Regenerated state** — `instruction-lock.toml`. Don't hand-edit; it is
  rewritten on every `agentrail instructions apply`, so any local changes
  are overwritten silently.
- **User config** — `instruction-profile.toml`. This is normal user-edited
  config, like `.gitconfig` or a `package.json`. Hand-edit it freely, or
  use `agentrail instructions profile *` subcommands to mutate via
  commands (which validate field values and surface typos).

## Working a branch in parallel with another agent

If another agent is working this same repo on its own branch at the same
time, you are both writing into `.agentrail/`. Step numbers are
per-branch and *will* collide — you will both have a `003-` — so your
step directories land on identical paths and the merge conflicts. The
**slug** is the only part that can keep the two lanes apart.

Pick a lane prefix naming your slice of the work (`rtx5060`, `rtx3060`,
`api`, `ui`) and namespace your saga with it:

```bash
agentrail rename prefix <lane> --dry-run   # preview, changes nothing
agentrail rename prefix <lane>             # apply
git add -A .agentrail/                     # -A: a dir move is a delete + an add
git commit -m "saga: rename into <lane> lane"
```

`001-setup` becomes `001-<lane>-setup`, and the saga name is prefixed
too. Your directories no longer collide with the other agent's, so both
lanes survive the merge.

**Run it retroactively — that is what it is for.** You do not need to
decide on a lane before starting work. Renaming is not renumbering: step
numbers, statuses, completion timestamps, and recorded commits are all
preserved, so steps you have already completed keep their git-history
linkage and `agentrail audit` still matches them. Unlike `insert` and
`reorder`, which refuse to touch completed steps, `rename` is safe on
work that has already landed.

It is also **idempotent** — steps already carrying the prefix are
skipped — so just re-run it whenever you have added steps.

**Archive your lane before the merge.** Slug prefixing separates the step
directories, but both branches still have a single `saga.toml` and
overlapping step numbers, so merging two *live* lanes still conflicts.
When your lane is done:

```bash
agentrail complete --summary "..." --done
agentrail archive --reason "<lane> lane merged upstream"
```

Because the saga name was prefixed too, the archive directories are
distinct and the merge is completely conflict-free, with both lanes'
histories landing side by side.

Finer-grained forms: `agentrail rename step <N> <new-slug>` renames one
step, `agentrail rename saga <new-name>` renames only the saga.

## Branch handoff after `agentrail complete`

Once a feature branch is committed and `agentrail complete` has run,
signal that it is ready for review/merge by renaming it from
`feat/<slug>` to `pr/<slug>`:

```bash
git branch -m feat/<slug> pr/<slug>
```

The rename is a useful convention regardless of how this project
handles handoff:

- It distinguishes "in-progress work" from "awaiting review" in the
  output of `git branch`.
- Project-specific tooling (CI, release-engineer scans, automated PR
  creation) can key off the `pr/*` prefix.
- It keeps the branch name stable across the review cycle even if the
  feature slug evolves.

What happens after the rename depends on what push capability you
have. See `push-discipline.md` for how to detect capability before
trying.

- **You can push and use GitHub PRs.** Push the renamed branch and
  open the PR:
  ```bash
  git push -u origin pr/<slug>
  gh pr create
  ```
  (Or push and open the PR via the web UI.)
- **You cloned via HTTPS without push access to the upstream remote.**
  Typical when contributing to an open-source project you don't own:
  push the renamed branch to your fork instead, then open the PR
  pointing at upstream. `git remote -v` shows your remotes; add a
  fork remote with `git remote add fork <url>` if needed.
- **Your project has a project-specific handoff flow** (release
  engineer scanning for `pr/*` branches, automated PR creation, CI
  hooks). The rename IS the handoff signal. Look for site-specific
  guidance in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md outside the briefing markers — if
  present, follow that instead.

After the rename, do not continue committing to `pr/<slug>` — those
commits will not be in the PR. Start further work on a fresh branch
off the (eventually merged and pulled) base.

## Push discipline

When you push (typically after `branch-handoff` has renamed `feat/X`
to `pr/X` and you're publishing the PR branch), do it safely.

### Verify push capability before assuming it works

- `git remote get-url origin` — `git@…` (SSH) or `https://…` plus a
  configured credential helper is push-capable. A bare `https://…`
  with no helper usually is not (read-only mirror or fresh clone).
- `gh auth status` — if the project uses GitHub PRs and `gh` is not
  authenticated, `gh pr create` will fail.
- `git push --dry-run` — surfaces auth or branch-protection problems
  without changing remote state.

### If you cannot push (or push fails)

- Note the unpushed branch state explicitly in your `agentrail
  complete --summary` so the next session knows the work is local.
- Do NOT silently leave commits stranded on a local branch — the next
  agent will look at the remote and assume your work was lost.
- Do NOT retry the same `git push` in a loop. If the failure is a
  permission issue (no SSH key, no `gh` auth, sandboxed user), retries
  will not fix it. Surface the failure to the user.
- If this project has a project-specific handoff flow (release
  engineer scans for `pr/*` branches, queue files, CI hooks
  documented in CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md outside the briefing markers),
  follow that instead of pushing — the branch rename from
  `branch-handoff.md` may already be sufficient.

### If the remote rejects a push

- For non-fast-forward errors on a personal branch, prefer
  `git pull --rebase` over `--force` unless the user has explicitly
  authorized force-push.
- Never force-push to a shared branch (`main`, release branches)
  without an explicit instruction.
- Never amend a commit that has already been pushed to a shared
  branch.

## Recovery: detecting and repairing saga/git drift

The saga is a record of git history. When the two diverge — agent forgets
to commit `.agentrail/`, a step is reverted, files are renamed by hand —
agentrail provides two recovery tools.

### Work done where the cursor never goes

A step finished in another lane, branch or repository stays `pending`
here, and once the cursor has passed it nothing brings the cursor back
(`agentrail status` lists such steps as **stranded**). Correct the record
with commands, never by hand-editing step.toml or by `reopen`-ing a
neighbor (that rewrites the neighbor's history):

```bash
agentrail close N --summary "..." --commit REF        # done in this repo
agentrail close N --summary "..." --elsewhere WHERE   # done elsewhere
agentrail edit N --prompt "..."          # a step not yet done, plan changed
agentrail reserve N --for OWNER          # someone else's: the cursor skips it
agentrail unreserve N                    # take it back
```

Reserve a step when you hand it off, before work starts, so it is never
stranded; `close` it when the owner reports it done.

### `agentrail audit`

Compares first-parent git history against saga steps and reports gaps.
Default output is a markdown report; `--emit-commands` prints a shell
script of `agentrail add` lines pre-seeded from commit subjects:

```bash
agentrail audit                    # human-readable report
agentrail audit --emit-commands    # draft script (review before running)
agentrail audit --since HEAD~50    # limit scope
```

The emitted script is a draft — slugs and prompts come from commit
subjects and usually need rewording. Review and edit before executing.

### `agentrail snapshot` (belt-and-suspenders)

Captures `.agentrail/` (and `.agentrail-archive/` if present) into a real
git commit under `refs/agentrail/snapshots/<timestamp>`. The blobs are
reachable, survive `git gc`, and can be restored with a normal git
command:

```bash
agentrail snapshot                 # take a snapshot now
agentrail snapshot --list          # list existing refs
git restore --source=<ref> -- .agentrail .agentrail-archive
```

Run a snapshot before risky agent operations or after creating files
you haven't yet staged. It does NOT replace normal git tracking — it is
a safety net for what is not yet committed.

## Git hygiene

- Never amend a commit that has already been pushed to a shared branch.
- Never use `--no-verify` to skip pre-commit hooks unless explicitly told to.
  If a hook fails, fix the underlying issue.
- Prefer naming files explicitly (`git add path/to/file`) over `git add -A`,
  to avoid sweeping in unintended files (secrets, local scratch, etc.).
- Resolve merge conflicts; do not discard changes by default.

## Project overview

reva-fork runs Ron Aaron's Reva Forth (`src/reva.f`, release 2011.2) on
a portable core: vx86, an IA-32-subset virtual machine in Rust, with
the original core's routines as Rust "gates". Hosts: the `reva` CLI,
a WebAssembly build for the browser, `reva-serve`, and a Tauri desktop
app. Version scheme `YYYY.MMDD.N` (see `rust/reva-vm/src/version.rs`):
the day's version is set once (`.0`) and all of that day's work stays on
it; `.1`, `.2` ... only for another release shipped to `main` the same
day. Bump only when the user asks.

Read before working:

- `README.md`, `docs/README.md` -- what exists and the doc index
- `rust/DESIGN.md` -- architecture, deviations, roadmap
- `docs/parity.md` -- what runs, what does not, decisions
- `.agentrail/plan.md` -- the current saga

Layout: `rust/` (workspace: reva-vm, reva-cli, reva-web, reva-serve),
`desktop/` (its own workspace: reva-desktop), `src/reva.f`, `lib/`
(Forth libraries, embedded into the VM), `examples/`, `docs/`,
`rust/work/reg-rs/` (goldens), `rust/scripts/`, `justfile`.

## Lanes

Two agents work this repository:

- **local** (this Mac): sw-checklist conformance, bugs, features, and
  verification on macOS, which the cloud cannot run. Saga steps carry
  the `local-` prefix.
- **cloud**: CoSy, reva-fork's main user, here and in
  `ba-cosy-zip-fork`. It does not use this saga.

The local lane does not edit `ba-cosy-zip-fork`. Tell the user before
moving or renaming files the cloud lane edits (most of `rust/reva-vm`),
so the cloud lane can rebase.

## Invariants

- `src/reva.f` stays verbatim. What the port needs is inserted at boot
  by `rust/reva-vm/src/embedded.rs`.
- Gate numbers (`rust/reva-vm/src/gates.rs`) are append-only: saved
  images hold gate addresses.
- Refactors change no behaviour: tests, goldens and the web smoke test
  pass unchanged.
- A golden is a claim that the output is correct: review every diff
  before `reg-rs rebase`.
- No GPL-family code or crates (`rust/scripts/license-check.sh`,
  `docs/licenses.md`).

## The gate

`just check` (`rust/scripts/check.sh`) before every commit: fmt and
clippy `-D warnings` and tests in `rust/` and `desktop/`, the wasm build
and its node tests, the goldens on the release CLI, the license check,
and sw-checklist. `just check --fast` skips the desktop workspace.

The script lists goldens known to fail per OS and the most sw-checklist
FAILs allowed. Both may only shrink: lower them in the commit that
fixes something, never raise them.

Tools it needs on PATH: `reg-rs`, `sed-rs`, `sw-checklist`, `node`,
`just`; the `wasm32-unknown-unknown` target.

## Workflow

- One PR to `dev` per saga step, from `feat/<slug>`, renamed to
  `pr/<slug>` at handoff. `main` is updated from `dev` by the user.
- Commit messages: a subject line, a blank line, then what changed and
  why; end with the Co-Authored-By line.
- Every commit adds its line to `CHANGES.md` (newest first, under the
  day, Pacific time, a category from its header), in the same commit;
  saga records and merges too. A PR's merge line is added by the next
  commit on `dev`.
- Scripts run on macOS's bash 3.2 and BSD tools as well as Linux.

- [Shared Mac: don't steal focus](shared-mac-no-focus-stealing.md) — never raise windows; capture by window ID
- [Code structure rules](code-structure-rules.md) — move out not combine; <=4 modules/crate, <=4 crates/workspace; facade lib.rs; tests out of src

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# Pre-commit gate, run SERIALLY -- one cargo at a time, via serial.sh's
# global lock (so it can never deadlock against a build or another gate).
#
#   scripts/gate.sh <workspace-dir> <pkg> [pkg...]
#
# <workspace-dir> is the component workspace that owns the packages (this
# repo has no root Cargo.toml; cargo -p must run inside the owning
# workspace, e.g. components/web-demos). For the named packages it runs
# rustfmt --check, clippy -D warnings, and `cargo test`, then sw-checklist.
#
# IMPORTANT: tests must NOT do heavy CPU training (it is slow and wasteful);
# keep interpreter-loop / GPU-fallback training demos out of the default
# test path (see SKIP_DEMOS in the web-demos registry test).

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
SERIAL="$SCRIPT_DIR/serial.sh"

if [ "$#" -lt 2 ]; then
    echo "usage: scripts/gate.sh <workspace-dir> <pkg> [pkg...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi

WS="$1"; shift
PKG_ARGS=()
for p in "$@"; do PKG_ARGS+=(-p "$p"); done

cd "$WS"
echo "=== Cargo.lock consistency ==="
# A stale lock here means a manifest changed (possibly in ANOTHER
# workspace this one path-depends on) without the lock being
# regenerated -- fix with scripts/check-locks.sh --fix.
"$SERIAL" cargo metadata --locked --format-version 1 >/dev/null

echo "=== rustfmt --check (${*}) ==="
"$SERIAL" cargo fmt "${PKG_ARGS[@]}" -- --check

echo "=== clippy -D warnings (${*}) ==="
"$SERIAL" cargo clippy "${PKG_ARGS[@]}" --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings

echo "=== cargo test (${*}) ==="
"$SERIAL" cargo test "${PKG_ARGS[@]}"

echo "=== sw-checklist ==="
sw-checklist 2>&1 | grep -iE 'Summary' || true

echo "=== gate OK ==="

content.content:
Insert a new pending step at a chosen position, shifting later steps up

Use when a bug or unplanned task needs to slot in before existing pending work. The new step lands at position `after + 1`; every pending/in-progress step with a number greater than `after` shifts up by one (step.toml `number` and the on-disk `NNN-slug` directory name are both updated). The operation is refused if any step that would shift is already `Completed`, since completed steps anchor git-tracked history.

Pass `--after 0` to prepend at position 1 (only works if step 1 is pending).

Cursor semantic (preemption): if the new step lands at or before the current cursor, focus follows the new arrival — the inserted step becomes `current_step` and the previously focused step is pushed to `current_step + 1`. This matches the "drop in a blocker" use case. If the new step lands behind the cursor, focus is unchanged and the new step is queued as future work.

Usage: agentrail insert [OPTIONS] --after <AFTER> --slug <SLUG> --prompt <PROMPT>

Options:
      --after <AFTER>
          Position to insert after (0 prepends). The new step becomes N+1

      --slug <SLUG>
          Slug for the new step

      --prompt <PROMPT>
          Step prompt: text, file path, or "-" for stdin

# justfile: common builds, as `just RECIPE` (https://just.systems).
# Every recipe is a thin wrapper over a script in rust/scripts/ or desktop/,
# so nothing here needs just: the script lines below work as they are.
#
#   just              list the recipes
#   just web-zip      the static site zip (rust/target/web/reva-web-VERSION.zip)

# list the recipes
default:
    @just --list

# the WebAssembly VM (rust/reva-web/www/reva.wasm)
wasm:
    rust/scripts/build-web.sh

# the browser REPL as an uploadable static zip; extra args go to make-web-zip.sh (--package DIR, --canvas MODE, ...)
web-zip *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/make-web-zip.sh {{ARGS}}

# publish the live demo (plain reva-fork, from main) to gh-pages; --dry-run builds without pushing
publish *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/publish-pages.sh {{ARGS}}

# serve the browser REPL from the source tree at http://localhost:8000/?canvas=split
web-dev: wasm
    python3 -m http.server -d rust/reva-web/www 8000

# reva-serve, the one-binary local web app, for this machine (or TARGETs: mac, linux, windows); args go to build-serve.sh
serve-build *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/build-serve.sh {{ARGS}}

# build reva-serve for this machine from the source tree and run it (opens the browser; Ctrl-C stops)
serve:
    cd rust && cargo run --release -p reva-serve

# the CLI (rust/target/release/reva)
cli:
    cd rust && cargo build --release -p reva-cli

# the desktop app (desktop/target/release/reva-desktop)
desktop:
    desktop/build.sh

# the gate before every commit: fmt, clippy, tests, goldens, licenses, sw-checklist (--fast skips the desktop)
check *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/check.sh {{ARGS}}

# timing guard for refactors of hot code: medians vs this host's baseline (--record to set it)
bench-guard *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/bench-guard.sh {{ARGS}}

# tests of the portable core and the browser build
test: wasm
    cd rust && cargo test --release --workspace
    node rust/reva-web/test/smoke.mjs
    node rust/reva-web/test/lineedit.mjs
    node rust/reva-web/test/ansi.mjs

# justfile: common builds, as `just RECIPE` (https://just.systems).
# Every recipe is a thin wrapper over a script in rust/scripts/ or desktop/,
# so nothing here needs just: the script lines below work as they are.
#
#   just              list the recipes
#   just web-zip      the static site zip (rust/target/web/reva-web-VERSION.zip)

# list the recipes
default:
    @just --list

# the WebAssembly VM (rust/reva-web/www/reva.wasm)
wasm:
    rust/scripts/build-web.sh

# the browser REPL as an uploadable static zip; extra args go to make-web-zip.sh (--package DIR, --canvas MODE, ...)
web-zip *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/make-web-zip.sh {{ARGS}}

# publish the live demo (plain reva-fork, from main) to gh-pages; --dry-run builds without pushing
publish *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/publish-pages.sh {{ARGS}}

# serve the browser REPL from the source tree at http://localhost:8000/?canvas=split
web-dev: wasm
    python3 -m http.server -d rust/reva-web/www 8000

# reva-serve, the one-binary local web app, for this machine (or TARGETs: mac, linux, windows); args go to build-serve.sh
serve-build *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/build-serve.sh {{ARGS}}

# build reva-serve for this machine from the source tree and run it (opens the browser; Ctrl-C stops)
serve:
    cd rust && cargo run --release -p reva-serve

# the CLI (rust/target/release/reva)
cli:
    cd rust && cargo build --release -p reva-cli

# the desktop app (desktop/target/release/reva-desktop)
desktop:
    desktop/build.sh

# the gate before every commit: fmt, clippy, tests, goldens, licenses, sw-checklist (--fast skips the desktop)
check *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/check.sh {{ARGS}}

# timing guard for refactors of hot code: medians vs this host's baseline (--record to set it)
bench-guard *ARGS:
    rust/scripts/bench-guard.sh {{ARGS}}

# tests of the portable core and the browser build
test: wasm
    cd rust && cargo test --release --workspace
    node rust/reva-web/test/smoke.mjs
    node rust/reva-web/test/lineedit.mjs
    node rust/reva-web/test/ansi.mjs

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The gate: everything that must pass before a commit (`just check`).
#
#   rust/scripts/check.sh            all of it
#   rust/scripts/check.sh --fast     skip the desktop workspace (Tauri)
#
# Runs, and stops at the first failure:
#   1. rust/: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests (release)
#   2. the WebAssembly build and its node tests
#   3. desktop/: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests
#   4. the reg-rs goldens on the release CLI; a failure is accepted only
#      if KNOWN_FAILURES lists it for this OS
#   5. the license check
#   6. sw-checklist: its FAIL count may not exceed SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS /bin/bash).
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"

# Goldens known to fail, per OS, until the step that fixes them
# (.agentrail: local-portable-gates).  The list may only shrink.
case "$(uname)" in
    Darwin) KNOWN_FAILURES="docs-samples" ;;
    *)      KNOWN_FAILURES="" ;;
esac

# sw-checklist FAILs: 51 on 2026-10-26, 49 after edition 2024, 47 after
# the web checks.  Lower this as steps fix them
# (.agentrail: local-edition-2024 ... local-split-front-ends); at 0 the
# checklist is required outright.
SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS=46

fast=0
[[ "${1:-}" == --fast ]] && fast=1

step() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\ncheck: FAILED: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

step "rust: fmt, clippy, tests"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "rust: cargo fmt --check (run cargo fmt)"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "rust: clippy"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo test -q --release --workspace) || fail "rust: tests"

step "web: wasm build, node tests"
"$root/rust/scripts/build-web.sh" >/dev/null || fail "web: build-web.sh"
for t in smoke lineedit ansi; do
    node "$root/rust/reva-web/test/$t.mjs" >/dev/null || fail "web: test/$t.mjs (run it for details)"
done

if [[ $fast -eq 0 ]]; then
    step "desktop: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "desktop: cargo fmt --check"
    "$root/desktop/build.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "desktop: build.sh (run it for details)"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "desktop: clippy"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo test -q --workspace) || fail "desktop: tests"
fi

step "goldens (reg-rs, release CLI)"
out=$(cd "$root/rust" && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh 2>&1) || true
echo "$out" | grep -E 'passed|FAIL' || fail "goldens: no summary from regress.sh"
unexpected=""
for t in $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *FAIL: *//p'); do
    case " $KNOWN_FAILURES " in
        *" $t "*) echo "   (known failure on $(uname): $t)" ;;
        *)        unexpected="$unexpected $t" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -z "$unexpected" ]] || fail "goldens:$unexpected (details: cd rust && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh -v -p NAME)"

step "licenses"
"$root/rust/scripts/license-check.sh" || fail "license-check.sh"

step "sw-checklist"
# sw-checklist exits 1 while it has FAILs; the count below is the test.
summary=$(cd "$root" && { sw-checklist 2>&1 || true; } | grep '^Summary:') || fail "sw-checklist did not run"
echo "$summary"
fails=$(echo "$summary" | sed -n 's/.* \([0-9][0-9]*\) failed.*/\1/p')
[[ -n "$fails" ]] || fail "sw-checklist: cannot read the FAIL count"
[[ "$fails" -le "$SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS" ]] ||
    fail "sw-checklist: $fails FAILs, more than $SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS (sw-checklist -v | grep FAIL)"

printf '\ncheck: ok\n'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the reg-rs regression suite for the portable Reva core.
#
#   scripts/regress.sh            build, then run every test (summary)
#   scripts/regress.sh -v         ... with failure details (-vv: full diffs)
#   scripts/regress.sh -p NAME    ... only tests matching NAME
#
# Needs reg-rs (https://github.com/sw-cli-tools/reg-rs) on PATH, or $REG_RS
# pointing at the binary.  Tests run from rust/ against $REVA (default: the
# debug build), so the same suite checks debug and release builds:
#   REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
REG_RS="${REG_RS:-$(command -v reg-rs || true)}"
if [[ -z "$REG_RS" ]]; then
    echo "regress: reg-rs not found; install it or set REG_RS" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [[ "${REVA:-target/debug/reva}" == target/release/reva ]]; then
    cargo build -q --release -p reva-cli
else
    cargo build -q -p reva-cli
fi
export REG_RS_DATA_DIR="$PWD/work/reg-rs"
exec "$REG_RS" run "$@"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# License gate: keep copyleft code and unreviewed binaries out of the tree.
#
#   scripts/license-check.sh          (from rust/; checks the whole repository)
#
# 1. No tracked file may carry GPL, LGPL or AGPL license text.
# 2. Every tracked binary (ELF, PE, Mach-O, object file, archive) must be on
#    the reviewed list below, with its license.  Each listed path must also
#    appear in docs/licenses.md, so the inventory and the gate cannot drift.
# 3. If cargo-deny is installed, `cargo deny check licenses` must pass in
#    each Cargo workspace (rust/deny.toml, desktop/deny.toml hold the lists).  Without it, a note is printed.
#
# Only git-tracked files are checked, so build output never trips the gate.
# Exit 1 on any failure.  Works with the bash 3.2 that macOS ships.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
status=0
fail() { echo "license-check: $*"; status=1; }

# Reviewed binaries: path, then license (see docs/licenses.md for the source
# of each judgement).  Adding a binary means reviewing it and adding it here.
# Read with `read -d ''`, not `$(cat <<EOF ...)`: bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash)
# mis-parses a here-document inside `$( )` when the text has an apostrophe.
read -r -d '' reviewed <<'EOF' || true
legacy/bin/lin/build                    Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/lin/core                     Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/lin/reva                     Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/lin/libimath.so              IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/lin/libiupall.so             IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/lin/shabal.so                Reva scratch, Ron Aaron (presumed public domain)
legacy/bin/mac/build                    Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/core                     Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/reva                     Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/libcd.dylib              CD (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libcdcontextplus.dylib   CD (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libcdgdk.dylib           CD (MIT); links the system GDK
legacy/bin/mac/libfreetype.dylib        FreeType (FTL, chosen from FTL/GPL-2.0)
legacy/bin/mac/libimath.dylib           IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiup.dylib             IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupcd.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupcontrols.dylib     IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupgl.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupim.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupimglib.dylib       IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/build.exe                Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/core.exe                 Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/reva.exe                 Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/curl.dll                 curl (curl license, MIT-style)
legacy/bin/win/glut32.dll               GLUT for Win32 (GLUT license: redistributable, not open source)
legacy/bin/win/imath.dll                IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/iupall.dll               IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/libexpat.dll             Expat (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/pcre.dll                 PCRE (BSD)
legacy/bin/win/pdcurses.dll             PDCurses (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/rss_process.dll          rss_process, Reinhold Software (permissive, see contrib/rss_process.zip)
legacy/bin/win/sqlite3.dll              SQLite (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/sqlite3.exe              SQLite (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/zlib1.dll                zlib (zlib)
legacy/src/revares.o                    Reva Windows resources (public domain)
legacy/scratch/mevarchim                Reva turnkey program (public domain)
legacy/scratch/zemanim                  Reva turnkey program (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1                     SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1b                    SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1c                    SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1transform.o          SHA-1 trial (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha/sha1                 SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha/sha1a                SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha/sha1transform.o      SHA-1 trial (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha/sha.zip              archive of legacy/scratch/sha (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1hash/upx-dialog.exe  SHA-1 dialog demo, axm 2003 (terms unknown; UPX-packed)
contrib/rss_process.zip                 rss_process sources, Reinhold Software (permissive)
EOF
is_reviewed() { echo "$reviewed" | awk '{print $1}' | grep -qxF -- "$1"; }

# Binary by content (magic numbers) or by extension, so a renamed file is caught.
is_binary() {
    case "$1" in
        *.dll|*.so|*.so.*|*.dylib|*.exe|*.o|*.a|*.lib|*.zip|*.gz|*.tgz|*.tar|*.bz2|*.xz|*.7z|*.jar) return 0 ;;
    esac
    local magic
    magic=$(head -c4 -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    case "$magic" in
        7f454c46|4d5a*|cffaedfe|cefaedfe|feedface|feedfacf|cafebabe|504b0304) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# This script names the pattern without being under it, so it is exempt.
copyleft='GNU (Lesser |Library |Affero )?General Public License|SPDX-License-Identifier:.*(GPL|AGPL)'
hits=$(git ls-files -z -- . ':!rust/scripts/license-check.sh' \
       | xargs -0 grep -l -a -E "$copyleft" 2>/dev/null || true)
for f in $hits; do fail "$f: GPL-family license text"; done

nbin=0
while IFS= read -r f; do
    [[ -f "$f" && ! -L "$f" ]] || continue
    is_binary "$f" || continue
    nbin=$((nbin+1))
    is_reviewed "$f" || fail "$f: binary not on the reviewed list (review it, then add it to this script and docs/licenses.md)"
done < <(git ls-files)

for f in $(echo "$reviewed" | awk '{print $1}'); do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || fail "$f: on the reviewed list but not in the tree (remove it from the list)"
    grep -qF -- "\`$f\`" docs/licenses.md || fail "$f: missing from docs/licenses.md"
done

if command -v cargo-deny >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for ws in rust desktop; do
        (cd "$ws" && cargo deny --log-level error check licenses >/dev/null) \
            || fail "$ws: cargo deny check licenses failed (run it in $ws/ for details)"
    done
    crates="crates checked by cargo-deny in rust/ and desktop/"
else
    crates="cargo-deny not installed: crate licenses not checked (cargo install cargo-deny)"
fi

if [[ $status -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "license-check: ok ($nbin reviewed binaries, no GPL-family text; $crates)"
fi
exit $status

    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "desktop: cargo fmt --check"
    "$root/desktop/build.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "desktop: build.sh (run it for details)"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "desktop: clippy"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo test -q --workspace) || fail "desktop: tests"
fi

step "goldens (reg-rs, release CLI)"
out=$(cd "$root/rust" && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh 2>&1) || true
echo "$out" | grep -E 'passed|FAIL' || fail "goldens: no summary from regress.sh"
unexpected=""
for t in $(echo "$out" | sed -n 's/^ *FAIL: *//p'); do
    case " $KNOWN_FAILURES " in
        *" $t "*) echo "   (known failure on $(uname): $t)" ;;
        *)        unexpected="$unexpected $t" ;;
    esac
done
[[ -z "$unexpected" ]] || fail "goldens:$unexpected (details: cd rust && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh -v -p NAME)"

step "licenses"
"$root/rust/scripts/license-check.sh" || fail "license-check.sh"

step "sw-checklist"
# sw-checklist exits 1 while it has FAILs; the count below is the test.
summary=$(cd "$root" && { sw-checklist 2>&1 || true; } | grep '^Summary:') || fail "sw-checklist did not run"
echo "$summary"
fails=$(echo "$summary" | sed -n 's/.* \([0-9][0-9]*\) failed.*/\1/p')
[[ -n "$fails" ]] || fail "sw-checklist: cannot read the FAIL count"
[[ "$fails" -le "$SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS" ]] ||
    fail "sw-checklist: $fails FAILs, more than $SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS (sw-checklist -v | grep FAIL)"

printf '\ncheck: ok\n'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run the reg-rs regression suite for the portable Reva core.
#
#   scripts/regress.sh            build, then run every test (summary)
#   scripts/regress.sh -v         ... with failure details (-vv: full diffs)
#   scripts/regress.sh -p NAME    ... only tests matching NAME
#
# Needs reg-rs (https://github.com/sw-cli-tools/reg-rs) on PATH, or $REG_RS
# pointing at the binary.  Tests run from rust/ against $REVA (default: the
# debug build), so the same suite checks debug and release builds:
#   REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
REG_RS="${REG_RS:-$(command -v reg-rs || true)}"
if [[ -z "$REG_RS" ]]; then
    echo "regress: reg-rs not found; install it or set REG_RS" >&2
    exit 2
fi
if [[ "${REVA:-target/debug/reva}" == target/release/reva ]]; then
    cargo build -q --release -p reva-cli
else
    cargo build -q -p reva-cli
fi
export REG_RS_DATA_DIR="$PWD/work/reg-rs"
exec "$REG_RS" run "$@"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# License gate: keep copyleft code and unreviewed binaries out of the tree.
#
#   scripts/license-check.sh          (from rust/; checks the whole repository)
#
# 1. No tracked file may carry GPL, LGPL or AGPL license text.
# 2. Every tracked binary (ELF, PE, Mach-O, object file, archive) must be on
#    the reviewed list below, with its license.  Each listed path must also
#    appear in docs/licenses.md, so the inventory and the gate cannot drift.
# 3. If cargo-deny is installed, `cargo deny check licenses` must pass in
#    each Cargo workspace (rust/deny.toml, desktop/deny.toml hold the lists).  Without it, a note is printed.
#
# Only git-tracked files are checked, so build output never trips the gate.
# Exit 1 on any failure.  Works with the bash 3.2 that macOS ships.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
status=0
fail() { echo "license-check: $*"; status=1; }

# of each judgement).  Adding a binary means reviewing it and adding it here.
# Read with `read -d ''`, not `$(cat <<EOF ...)`: bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash)
# mis-parses a here-document inside `$( )` when the text has an apostrophe.
read -r -d '' reviewed <<'EOF' || true

legacy/bin/lin/core                     Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/lin/reva                     Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/lin/libimath.so              IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/lin/libiupall.so             IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/lin/shabal.so                Reva scratch, Ron Aaron (presumed public domain)
legacy/bin/mac/build                    Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/core                     Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/reva                     Reva (public domain), UPX-packed
legacy/bin/mac/libcd.dylib              CD (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libcdcontextplus.dylib   CD (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libcdgdk.dylib           CD (MIT); links the system GDK
legacy/bin/mac/libfreetype.dylib        FreeType (FTL, chosen from FTL/GPL-2.0)
legacy/bin/mac/libimath.dylib           IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiup.dylib             IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupcd.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupcontrols.dylib     IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupgl.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupim.dylib           IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/mac/libiupimglib.dylib       IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/build.exe                Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/core.exe                 Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/reva.exe                 Reva (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/curl.dll                 curl (curl license, MIT-style)
legacy/bin/win/glut32.dll               GLUT for Win32 (GLUT license: redistributable, not open source)
legacy/bin/win/imath.dll                IMath (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/iupall.dll               IUP (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/libexpat.dll             Expat (MIT)
legacy/bin/win/pcre.dll                 PCRE (BSD)
legacy/bin/win/pdcurses.dll             PDCurses (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/rss_process.dll          rss_process, Reinhold Software (permissive, see contrib/rss_process.zip)
legacy/bin/win/sqlite3.dll              SQLite (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/sqlite3.exe              SQLite (public domain)
legacy/bin/win/zlib1.dll                zlib (zlib)
legacy/src/revares.o                    Reva Windows resources (public domain)
legacy/scratch/mevarchim                Reva turnkey program (public domain)
legacy/scratch/zemanim                  Reva turnkey program (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1                     SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1b                    SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha1c                    SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)

legacy/scratch/sha/sha1                 SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)
legacy/scratch/sha/sha1a                SHA-1 trial, Steve Reid's code (public domain)

legacy/scratch/sha1hash/upx-dialog.exe  SHA-1 dialog demo, axm 2003 (terms unknown; UPX-packed)
contrib/rss_process.zip                 rss_process sources, Reinhold Software (permissive)

is_reviewed() { echo "$reviewed" | awk '{print $1}' | grep -qxF -- "$1"; }

# Binary by content (magic numbers) or by extension, so a renamed file is caught.
is_binary() {
    case "$1" in
        *.dll|*.so|*.so.*|*.dylib|*.exe|*.o|*.a|*.lib|*.zip|*.gz|*.tgz|*.tar|*.bz2|*.xz|*.7z|*.jar) return 0 ;;
    esac
    local magic
    magic=$(head -c4 -- "$1" 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')
    case "$magic" in
        7f454c46|4d5a*|cffaedfe|cefaedfe|feedface|feedfacf|cafebabe|504b0304) return 0 ;;
    esac
    return 1
}

# This script names the pattern without being under it, so it is exempt.
copyleft='GNU (Lesser |Library |Affero )?General Public License|SPDX-License-Identifier:.*(GPL|AGPL)'
hits=$(git ls-files -z -- . ':!rust/scripts/license-check.sh' \
       | xargs -0 grep -l -a -E "$copyleft" 2>/dev/null || true)
for f in $hits; do fail "$f: GPL-family license text"; done

nbin=0
while IFS= read -r f; do
    [[ -f "$f" && ! -L "$f" ]] || continue
    is_binary "$f" || continue
    nbin=$((nbin+1))
    is_reviewed "$f" || fail "$f: binary not on the reviewed list (review it, then add it to this script and docs/licenses.md)"
done < <(git ls-files)

for f in $(echo "$reviewed" | awk '{print $1}'); do
    [[ -e "$f" ]] || fail "$f: on the reviewed list but not in the tree (remove it from the list)"
    grep -qF -- "\`$f\`" docs/licenses.md || fail "$f: missing from docs/licenses.md"
done

if command -v cargo-deny >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    for ws in rust desktop; do
        (cd "$ws" && cargo deny --log-level error check licenses >/dev/null) \
            || fail "$ws: cargo deny check licenses failed (run it in $ws/ for details)"
    done
    crates="crates checked by cargo-deny in rust/ and desktop/"
else
    crates="cargo-deny not installed: crate licenses not checked (cargo install cargo-deny)"
fi

if [[ $status -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "license-check: ok ($nbin reviewed binaries, no GPL-family text; $crates)"
fi
exit $status

# cargo-deny policy for the portable core: permissive licenses only.
#
#   cargo deny check licenses        (from rust/; run by scripts/license-check.sh)
#
# Why: everything this workspace builds is redistributed (CLI binary, wasm
# module, desktop app), and the project ships no GPL, LGPL or AGPL code.
# Any crate whose license is not on this list fails the check, including
# crates with no license metadata.  See docs/licenses.md.

[licenses]
version = 2
allow = [
    "MIT",
    "Apache-2.0",
    "Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception",
    "BSD-2-Clause",
    "BSD-3-Clause",
    "ISC",
    "Zlib",
    "Unicode-3.0",
    "CC0-1.0",
    "Unlicense",
]
confidence-threshold = 0.9
# The workspace has no dependencies yet; keep the list for the ones to come.
unused-allowed-license = "allow"

[licenses.private]
# Workspace crates (publish = false) are MIT, checked by review, not here.
ignore = true

[package]
name = "reva-desktop"
description = "Reva Forth desktop app: the browser REPL in a native window, with files on disk"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
publish.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
authors.workspace = true

[build-dependencies]
tauri-build = { version = "2", features = [] }

[dependencies]
tauri = { version = "2", features = [] }
# Decodes a package's icon; already in the tree through Tauri.
png = "0.18"
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
# SQLite for lib/db/sqlite (host calls), through rusqlite's safe API.
reva-sqlite = { path = "../../rust/reva-sqlite" }

# Sets the program name before GTK starts, so a package's `id` becomes the
# Wayland app_id / X11 WM_CLASS (see Branding in main.rs).  Already in the
# tree through Tauri's GTK stack, so it adds no crate.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
glib = "0.18"

# Sets the Dock icon from a package's icon (set_dock_icon in main.rs).  The
# same objc2 crates Tauri's macOS backend (tao, wry) already builds, with
# features it already enables, so it adds no crate.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
objc2 = "0.6"
objc2-app-kit = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["std", "NSApplication", "NSImage", "NSResponder"] }
objc2-foundation = { version = "0.3", default-features = false, features = ["std", "NSData"] }

import os,re

where={c:k for k,v in comps.items() for c in v}
where['reva-desktop']='desktop'
desc={'x86':'vx86, the IA-32-subset processor','host':'the host interface (Host, host calls, the virtual file system, embedded sources)','core':'the Machine, its run loop, and the machine_trait! macro','words':"the core's words: gate dispatch and the gate families",'vlib':'virtual libraries (libc, turtle, highlight, sqlite, iconv)','vm':'reva-vm, the facade the front ends use','cli':'the `reva` command-line REPL','web':'the WebAssembly build and the browser page (www/)','serve':'reva-serve, the one-binary local web app','sqlite':'SQLite for the native hosts, through rusqlite'}
profile='''
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
'''
for comp,crates in comps.items():
    members=', '.join(f'"crates/{c}"' for c in crates)
    extra=''
    if comp=='web': extra='\n[profile.release.package.reva-web]\nopt-level = "s"\n'
    open(f'components/{comp}/Cargo.toml','w').write(f'''# Component {comp}: {desc[comp]}.
# One Cargo workspace per component (docs/code-metrics.md); the build
# output goes to the repository's target/ (.cargo/config.toml).
[workspace]
resolver = "2"
members = [{members}]

[workspace.package]
version = "2026.1026.0"
edition = "2024"
publish = false
license = "MIT"
authors = ["Reva development team"]
rust-version = "1.89"
{profile}{extra}''')
# path deps
for crate,comp in where.items():
    p=f'components/{comp}/crates/{crate}/Cargo.toml'
    s=open(p).read()
    def rep(m):
        dep=m.group(1)
        dc=where[dep]
        return f'path = "../{dep}"' if dc==comp else f'path = "../../../{dc}/crates/{dep}"'
    s=re.sub(r'path = "(?:\.\./)+(?:rust/)?(reva-[a-z0-9]+)"',rep,s)
    open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

desc={'x86':'vx86, the IA-32-subset processor','host':'the host interface (Host, host calls, the virtual file system, embedded sources)','core':'the Machine, its run loop, and the machine_trait! macro','words':"the core's words: gate dispatch and the gate families",'vlib':'virtual libraries (libc, turtle, highlight, sqlite, iconv)','vm':'reva-vm, the facade the front ends use','cli':'the `reva` command-line REPL','web':'the WebAssembly build and the browser page (www/)','serve':'reva-serve, the one-binary local web app','sqlite':'SQLite for the native hosts, through rusqlite'}
profile='''
[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
lto = true
codegen-units = 1
panic = "abort"
'''
for comp,crates in comps.items():
    members=', '.join(f'"crates/{c}"' for c in crates)
    extra=''
    if comp=='web': extra='\n[profile.release.package.reva-web]\nopt-level = "s"\n'
    open(f'components/{comp}/Cargo.toml','w').write(f'''# Component {comp}: {desc[comp]}.

# output goes to the repository's target/ (.cargo/config.toml).
[workspace]
resolver = "2"
members = [{members}]

[workspace.package]
version = "2026.1026.0"
edition = "2024"
publish = false
license = "MIT"
authors = ["Reva development team"]
rust-version = "1.89"
{profile}{extra}''')
# path deps
for crate,comp in where.items():
    p=f'components/{comp}/crates/{crate}/Cargo.toml'
    s=open(p).read()
    def rep(m):
        dep=m.group(1)
        dc=where[dep]
        return f'path = "../{dep}"' if dc==comp else f'path = "../../../{dc}/crates/{dep}"'
    s=re.sub(r'path = "(?:\.\./)+(?:rust/)?(reva-[a-z0-9]+)"',rep,s)
    open(p,'w').write(s)

#!/bin/sh
# build-stamp.sh: print "VERSION COMMIT DATE" for this checkout, the value
# of the page's `reva-build` meta tag (shown in the About dialog).
#
#   VERSION  the workspace version (rust/Cargo.toml)
#   COMMIT   the short commit hash, with "-dirty" if tracked files changed
#   DATE     the commit's date (UTC), not today's, so a rebuild of the same
#            commit gives the same stamp
# Outside a git checkout: "VERSION unknown unknown".
set -eu
RUST=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
version=$(awk -F'"' '/^version *=/ { print $2; exit }' "$RUST/Cargo.toml")
commit=$(git -C "$RUST" rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
if [ "$commit" != unknown ] && ! git -C "$RUST" diff --quiet HEAD -- 2>/dev/null; then
    commit=$commit-dirty
fi
date=$(TZ=UTC git -C "$RUST" log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%d 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
echo "$version $commit ${date:-unknown}"
"""
import argparse, glob, html, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

LEXICAL = ("com", "stk", "str", "num", "colon", "def")
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

def default_tables():
    """reva-fork's lib/highlight/forth.tbl, then any *.tbl beside this script.

    The same script runs from reva-fork (rust/scripts/) and from a package
    such as ba-cosy-zip-fork (reva-fork-subset/, with reva-fork beside the
    checkout or named by $REVA_FORK); a package's own table sits beside it.
    """
    forth = [os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "lib", "highlight", "forth.tbl"),
             os.path.join(HERE, "..", "..", "reva-fork", "lib", "highlight", "forth.tbl")]
    if os.environ.get("REVA_FORK"):
        forth.insert(0, os.path.join(os.environ["REVA_FORK"], "lib", "highlight", "forth.tbl"))
    found = [p for p in forth if os.path.isfile(p)][:1]
    if not found:
        sys.exit("forth-highlight: reva-fork's lib/highlight/forth.tbl not found; "
                 "set REVA_FORK=/path/to/reva-fork or pass --table")
#                   could not load, ...)
#   timeout         still running after the time limit (interactive/looping)
# Area is a heuristic from the program's `needs` lines.
set -uo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
REVA="${REVA:-target/debug/reva}"
LIMIT="${PARITY_TIMEOUT:-5}"
# Text filters use sed-rs (https://github.com/sw-cli-tools/sed-rs), not the
# system sed, so they behave the same on macOS, Linux and Windows.
SED_RS="${SED_RS:-$(command -v sed-rs || true)}"
[[ -n "$SED_RS" ]] || { echo "parity-examples: sed-rs not found; install it or set SED_RS" >&2; exit 2; }
root=..
abs_root=$(cd "$root" && pwd)
# Programs that `save` write an image to the working directory, so each
# runs in a scratch directory, not in the checkout.
work=$(mktemp -d)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The gate: everything that must pass before a commit (`just check`).
#
#   rust/scripts/check.sh            all of it
#   rust/scripts/check.sh --fast     skip the desktop workspace (Tauri)
#
# Runs, and stops at the first failure:
#   1. rust/: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests (release)
#   2. the WebAssembly build and its node tests
#   3. desktop/: cargo fmt --check, clippy -D warnings, tests
#   4. the reg-rs goldens on the release CLI; a failure is accepted only
#      if KNOWN_FAILURES lists it for this OS
#   5. the license check
#   6. sw-checklist: its FAIL count may not exceed SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS
#
# Bash 3.2 compatible (macOS /bin/bash).
set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"

# Goldens known to fail, per OS, until the step that fixes them
# (.agentrail: local-portable-gates).  The list may only shrink.
case "$(uname)" in
    Darwin) KNOWN_FAILURES="docs-samples" ;;
    *)      KNOWN_FAILURES="" ;;
esac

# sw-checklist FAILs: 51 on 2026-10-26, 49 after edition 2024, 47 after
# the web checks.  Lower this as steps fix them
# (.agentrail: local-edition-2024 ... local-split-front-ends); at 0 the
# checklist is required outright.
SW_CHECKLIST_MAX_FAILS=46

fast=0
[[ "${1:-}" == --fast ]] && fast=1

step() { printf '\n== %s\n' "$*"; }
fail() { printf '\ncheck: FAILED: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

step "rust: fmt, clippy, tests"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "rust: cargo fmt --check (run cargo fmt)"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "rust: clippy"
(cd "$root/rust" && cargo test -q --release --workspace) || fail "rust: tests"

step "web: wasm build, node tests"
"$root/rust/scripts/build-web.sh" >/dev/null || fail "web: build-web.sh"
for t in smoke lineedit ansi; do
    node "$root/rust/reva-web/test/$t.mjs" >/dev/null || fail "web: test/$t.mjs (run it for details)"
done

if [[ $fast -eq 0 ]]; then
    step "desktop: fmt, clippy, tests"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo fmt --check) || fail "desktop: cargo fmt --check"
    "$root/desktop/build.sh" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "desktop: build.sh (run it for details)"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo clippy -q --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings) || fail "desktop: clippy"
    (cd "$root/desktop" && cargo test -q --workspace) || fail "desktop: tests"
fi

step "goldens (reg-rs, release CLI)"
out=$(cd "$root/rust" && REVA=target/release/reva scripts/regress.sh 2>&1) || true
echo "$out" | grep -E 'passed|FAIL' || fail "goldens: no summary from regress.sh"

## Code Metric Gates and Architecture Guide

This section guides AI coding agents in creating loosely-coupled, functional-style, testable, and maintainable Rust code that fits small-part complexity gates. The principles apply broadly across languages; the examples are Rust.

**Companion document: [`docs/loose-coupling.md`](loose-coupling.md)** captures the HOW: the four phases code can run in (compile time, start-up, conditional, dataflow pipeline) and the compose-don't-compress techniques (top-down delegation, separated stage definitions, iterator pipelines, building chains vs dispatching chains). When a function or module is over the budgets below, walk the four phases and split by phase -- do NOT compress with whitespace tricks or `rustfmt::skip`. The 25-LOC budget assumes idiomatic formatting.

### Target Metric Gates

| Level | Preferred Gate |
| --- | --- |
| Lines per function | <= 25 LOC |
| Functions per module | <= 5 |
| Modules per crate | <= 5 |
| Crates per component/workspace group | <= 5 |
| Major subsystems per repo | <= 5-ish |

**Guiding rule:** Every part should fit in human working memory. When a part grows, split by responsibility, not by accident. The 25-LOC function gate keeps a function on a single page view. The 5-per gate (mental load 5 +/- 2) reserves room for future expansion.

---

## Symptom -> technique (sw-checklist quick lookup)

When `sw-checklist` flags a specific issue, the lookup
below maps the warning category to the technique most
likely to retire it. Walk these first before inventing a
new approach.

### Function LOC over 25 (Function-LOC warning)

| Symptom | First-try technique |
|---------|---------------------|
| Function does steps A, B, C inline | Extract each into a named helper; orchestrator becomes 3 lines (top-down delegation). |
| Function has 2-3 nested loops | Replace with iterator pipeline (`.iter().map().filter().fold()`); each stage is a small named helper. |
| Function has 4+ `match` arms, each 10+ lines | Each arm becomes a named helper; the match becomes a dispatch. (Building-chains-vs-dispatching-chains.) |
| Function has 6+ argument-count / type checks at the top | Hoist into a macro (`check_arity!`, `check_kind!`); per-fn becomes one line. |
| Function builds a struct with 5+ fields | Builder pattern, or pre-build field values in let-bindings then construct in one line. |
| Function mixes parsing + validation + emission | Split by responsibility into `parse_*`, `validate_*`, `emit_*`; orchestrator chains them. |
| Function has `let mut` accumulator + push loop | `.iter().map(...).collect()` |
| Function has nested `match` on `Result`/`Option` | `?` operator + `and_then` chain. |

### Function LOC over 50 (Function-LOC FAIL)

Same techniques as above, just more of them. The
function is doing 3-4 things instead of 2. Walk the four
phases (compile-time / start-up / conditional / dataflow)
and identify which pieces belong where.

### Module function count over 7 (Module-Function-Count FAIL)

| Symptom | First-try technique |
|---------|---------------------|
| Several `impl Self` methods cluster by responsibility (data ops + render ops + validate ops) | Each cluster moves to a sibling `impl Self` block in its own file. Same struct, multiple `impl` blocks across files. |
| Same boilerplate-shaped fn repeats N times | Macro it; the per-fn definitions disappear into the macro expansion. |
| Production fns + test fns + test helpers in same file | Move tests + helpers to a sibling `mod.rs` / `tests/` file; production fn count drops by the test count. |
| One big dispatcher with N arm-handler fns | Split dispatcher into one file, arm handlers into a sibling file. |

### File LOC over 500 (File-LOC FAIL)

| Symptom | First-try technique |
|---------|---------------------|
| Pure data (static tables, lessons, demos) | Split by topic into sibling files (each holds one topical const). The "facade" file references them. |
| One struct with 20+ methods | Split methods into multiple `impl` blocks across sibling files. |
| Dispatcher + arm handlers in one file | Extract arm handlers to a sibling file. |
| Same module hosts builders + dispatchers + tests | Pull each phase to its own file (builders.rs, dispatch.rs, tests/). |

### Crate module count over 7 (Crate-Module-Count FAIL)

| Symptom | First-try technique |
|---------|---------------------|
| Many topically-different modules in one crate | Pull a topical cluster (5+ related modules) into a new sibling crate. Old crate becomes a facade depending on the new one. |
| Modules that group naturally already (`foo_a`, `foo_b`, `foo_c`) | New crate `mlpl-foo` absorbs them; the parent crate re-exports. |

### Clippy Allows attribute (Clippy-Allows FAIL)

The lint exists for a reason. Refactor the code to satisfy
it; never silence it with `#[allow(clippy::...)]` outside
vendored code.

| Clippy lint | Refactor |
|-------------|----------|
### 12. Suggested Repository Shape

```
repo/
  Cargo.toml
  crates/
    cli/
    core/
    report/
    rules/
    test-support/
  docs/
    architecture.md
    design.md
    metrics.md
  tests/
    cli_tests.rs
```

Possible crate roles:

| Crate | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `core` | Domain model and pure analysis |
| `rules` | Metric gates and validation policies |
| `report` | Markdown/JSON/terminal output |
| `cli` | Arg parsing, config loading, effectful shell |
| `test-support` | Fixtures and helpers |

---

### 13. `lib.rs` and `mod.rs` Are Facades Only

Do not put executable logic in `src/lib.rs`, `src/main.rs`, or any `src/foo/mod.rs`.

Allowed in `lib.rs` / `mod.rs`:

```rust
pub mod config;
pub mod rules;
pub mod report;

pub use config::Config;
pub use rules::RuleSet;
```

Not allowed:

```rust
pub fn analyze_repo(...) -> Result<Report> {
    ...
}
```

Instead:

```
src/
  lib.rs
  analysis/
    mod.rs
    analyze.rs
    plan.rs
```

```rust
// analysis/mod.rs
mod analyze;
mod plan;

pub use analyze::analyze_repo;
```

```rust
// analysis/analyze.rs
pub fn analyze_repo(...) -> Result<Report> {
    ...
}
```

**Rule:** `lib.rs` and `mod.rs` define the public surface. Named files contain behavior.

---

### 14. `build.rs` Follows the Same Rules
